cap: Estradiol and progesterone build the functionalis, which spiral arteries feed and menses sheds; the basalis, fed by straight arteries, survives and regrows it, so curettage into the basalis leaves Asherman adhesions. After ovulation the glands run a clock: subnuclear vacuoles at about 2 days, stromal edema near day 7 as the embryo implants, and predecidual cells later. Falling progesterone then releases prostaglandins, which spasm the spiral arteries and cause cramps.
